simple.meaning: יָאָה (yâʼâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be suitable.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Jeremiah, beginning at Jeremiah 10:7. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָאָה (H2969) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָאָה (yâʼâh) / H2969 is traced through Jeremiah 10:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2969. yaah [ יָאָה ] verb befit, be befitting (Late Hebrew יָאֶה יָאֵי, ᵑ7 adjective worthy, fitting, fine ; יָאוּת adverb right, well ; Phoenician יא fair ; Syriac adjective for נאוה Psa 33:1 , πρέπει Matt 3:15 ) — Qal Perfect יָאָ֑תָה לְךָ Jer 10:7 , for thee it (i.e. fear) is befitting , late Aramaism. יְאוֺר see יְאֹר . יַאֲזַנְיָה יַאֲזַנְיָ֫הוּ, see below אזן above יָאִירִי יָאִיר, see below אור above
